newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-SGB bullish on profit, unit mergers still on.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SGB bullish on profit, unit mergers still on.

text.p: Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB), Belgium's biggest holding company, is bullish on 1996 profit and is still looking at mergers of some of its units, SGB board chairman Etienne Davignon said on Thursday.
"I can confirm our October forecast that current and net 1996 profits will rise, that is now a fact," Davignon told Reuters in an interview.
In 1995, SGB's group net profit fell 16 percent to 9.21 billion francs.
"At the moment, all our businesses are doing well. 1997 already looks better than 1996," Davignon said.
But he also indicated SGB would keep its dividend on 1996 earnings unchanged from the 87 francs per share net paid on 1995 earnings. "I see no great reason for an increase of dividend."
Davignon also said that it was "technically possible" to consider an optional stock dividend.

Analysts have pointed out that SGB is loaded with 32 billion francs worth of debt following the increase of its stake in its Tractebel unit last year, while SGB's French parent company Compagnie de Suez is sitting on a cash pile of roughly the same size.
A stock dividend would be a way of keeping cash in SGB rather than moving it to Suez, which owns 62 percent of SGB.
"We are now in the situation that we can look at the possibility of an optional stock dividend," Davignon said.
He stressed a stock dividend had not been formally studied.

Davignon also said SGB will decide on a possible merger of its units Tractebel and Powerfin at the end of March. He declined to say whether it was certain that the merger between the two utility holding companies would go ahead.

Tractebel and its controlling shareholder SGB have been looking into the possibility of a full merger between Tractebel and Tractebel unit Powerfin since September, when SGB increased its stake in Tractebel to 65 percent.
Powerfin is the vehicle which spearheads Tractebel's expansion into utility services abroad.
Davignon also said that SGB is still interested in a possible merger between its unit Generale Bank and Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL).
But he added that the project was still blocked by Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING). Dutch ING is one of BBL's leading shareholders.
"At this moment, the project is in the freezer," he said.
"If anything would change, a merger between BBL and Generale Bank would still be a good business proposal and a project we would be happy to look at," he said.
The stock prices of BBL and Generale Bank flared at the start of last year, after Davignon said he backed the idea of creating one big Belgian bank.
But the merger project was abandoned in April 1996, following ING opposition against the plan.
ING has said it will defend its BBL stake but has never made clear if, under certain conditions, it would be willing to allow a merger. ING controls 20 percent of BBL stock.
